title: Cap. VIII Arg. 6 Ad primum: De bono perseverantiae — deserting God concerns common exciting grace
pass_a_gloss: To the first: When Augustine says that Men first desert God, and thence merit that they be deserted by God, he does not regard the negation of this grace which we call efficacious and special, and in the negation of which we assert this reprobation or passing by to be properly constituted; but the subtraction of a more common and exciting grace; which we confess is taken from men on account of demerits, yet so that without that prior preparation of the prior special grace, they would have fallen into this demerit of contumacy.
pass_b_english: To the first: when Augustine says men first desert God and thence merit to be deserted by God, he is not speaking of the denial of that efficacious special grace in whose denial we locate reprobation or praeterition proper. He means subtraction of a more common, exciting grace — which we grant is taken from men for demerits — yet so that without the prior preparation of that special grace they would already have fallen into this demerit of contumacy.
source_text: Ad primum: Quando Augustinus dicit, Homines prius deserere Deum, atque inde mereri ut deserantur a Deo, non spectat negationem hujus gratiae, quam efficacem et specialem vocamus, atque in hujus negatione hanc reprobationem sive praeteritionem proprie constitutam asserimus; sed gratiae communioris et excitantis subtractionem; quam fatemur propter demerita tolli hominibus, ita tamen ut sine praevia illa prioris gratiae specialis praeparatione, in hoc contumaciae demeritum incidissent.
